items.title: 67559_Art Hodes oral history interview
items.q: I'm sorry I didn't come in a little earlier, so I could have hung around with Joe Oliver.

ctx.x: I'm not going to say I'd do it all over you, like the joke. No, if I had to do it all over again, I'd consider myself one of the most fortunate people in the world that the direction that I took, that I stayed out of big bands, where I would have been -- I could learn how to play in big bands, it's not that difficult. I went for extra schooling one time for four years, practiced four hours a night, four to eight hours. I could have gone for whatever I needed and get it, if my interest was there.

But, oh, I made a lot of mistakes. It's ridiculous to say I would do it the same way. But basically, the way I followed the music, oh, there's no question about it. I'm sorry I didn't come in a little earlier, so I could have hung around with Joe Oliver. I missed some people. Just like, from where you sit or the next person sits, he wished he could come in ten years earlier because he missed some people. And he hated to have missed.

But when I came in, it was still the golden age of, not only jazz, but entertainment. We had Clayton Jackson Durrant. How many people caught an act in person? I did. And -- I mean, who are around. And I've become an antique. Look, he's still breathing. But I can --
